title: The χ² family as a named sampling law
dek: χ²_k is the law of a sum of k independent standard Normal squares. It is the reference for many LRTs, Pearson goodness-of-fit statistics, and sample variances — not a test by itself.
story: If Z₁, …, Z_k are iid N(0,1), then Q = ∑ Zⱼ² ~ χ²_k. The mean is k and the variance is 2k. The density is skewed for small k and looks more Normal as k grows (another CLT). This is a sampling law for a statistic, not a model for CFU.

Why software prints χ²: Wilks’ theorem sends 2Δℓ to χ² with df equal to the number of interior restrictions. Pearson’s X² = ∑ (O − E)²/E is asymptotically χ² under a correctly specified multinomial/Poisson model. A Gaussian sample variance: (n−1)s²/σ² ~ χ²_{n−1} in the iid Normal case. Three different statistics, one named family of references.

The distribution is not the test. A test is a rejection rule that uses a tail of this (or another) reference. Boundary LRTs, sparse tables, and sandwich-based “Wald χ²” with the wrong df are how the name gets ahead of the regularity.
deep: Degrees of freedom k is not “n − 1” by slogan. It is the rank of a quadratic form, or the number of independent restrictions, or the dimension gap in a nested MLE — say which.
Noncentral χ² appears in power calculations: if the Zⱼ have nonzero means, Q is noncentral with a noncentrality parameter that grows like n times a signal. Power of an LRT is not 1 − α.
Sums: independent χ²_a and χ²_b add to χ²_{a+b}. That is why nested deviance gaps add in exponential families when the restrictions stack.
t_ν is a Normal divided by √(χ²_ν/ν), independent numerator and denominator. z versus t is a Normal-versus-estimated-scale story, not a different philosophy of H₀.
Pearson X² with tiny expected counts does not wait for the χ² limit. Exact multinomial tests or a likelihood-ratio with simulation exist because the name on the printout is an approximation.

formulas.label: Wilks reference (regular, interior)

visual.caption: χ²_k as k grows: a right-skewed law at k = 2, a broader law at k = 6, and a more symmetric mound at large k. Mean equals k, so the curves sit farther right as df increase — they are not a single “chi-square test shape.”

example.title: Why Λ = 5.3 is not “χ² = 5.3 therefore p < 0.05” without k
example.setup: An LRT gives Λ = 2Δℓ = 5.3. One person looks up a χ²_1 5% point (3.84) and rejects. Another says the full model added two parameters and looks up χ²_2 (5.99) and does not reject.

steps.title: Name k
steps.body: If the extra terms were two free parameters with interior MLE and nested models, k = 2. P(χ²_2 ≥ 5.3) ≈ 0.07. If only one extra parameter, k = 1 and p ≈ 0.021. The statistic is the same; the reference is not.

steps.title: Regularity
steps.body: If one of those parameters was a variance on the boundary, neither χ²_1 nor χ²_2 is the null law. The name on the printout does not repair that.

steps.title: Print df
steps.body: A methods line “χ² p < 0.05” without k, without the restriction, and without the statistic is not a result.

example.takeaway: χ²_k is a family. The subscript is part of the name.

check.why: A sum of k independent unit-variance Normal squares has mean k. Variance is 2k.

whyWrong.2k: That is Var(Q), not the mean.
whyWrong.n − 1 always: That is df for an iid Normal sample variance, one use of the family, not the definition.

check.prompt: Z₁, Z₂ iid N(0,1). What is the law of Z₁² + Z₂²?
check.why: Definition of χ² with k = 2. Mean 2, not a Normal on the original scale.

whyWrong.N(0,2): The sum of the Z’s (not squares) would be N(0,2).
whyWrong.t_2: t needs a Normal divided by an independent χ²-based SD.

check.prompt: On the density plate, why do the curves sit farther right as the label’s k grows?
choices: Because larger df shrink the mean toward 0
Because E[χ²_k] = k, so the sampling law of the sum of more squared Normals is centred farther from 0
Because χ² is a probability of H₀
check.answer: Because E[χ²_k] = k, so the sampling law of the sum of more squared Normals is centred farther from 0
check.why: The plate is teaching a family of laws, not one sacred test shape.

whyWrong.Because χ² is a probability of H₀: χ² is a sampling law for a statistic.
whyWrong.Because software always uses k = 2: k is the restriction count or rank.
